chunks: What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Kūfī, whose لقب was Ḥamdān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I was sitting in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man entered and asked him about the takbīr over funerals. He said: Five takbīrs.
Then another entered and asked him about the salat over funerals, so he said to him: Four prayers.
The first said: May I be made your ransom, I asked you and you said five, and this one asked you and you said four.
So he said: You asked me about the takbīr, while this one asked me about the salat.

Then he said: It is five takbīrs, between them are four prayers. Then he spread his palm and said: They are five takbīrs, between them are four prayers. And we have fully covered what pertains to this chapter in our major book.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُ صَلَوَاتٍ: Four supplicatory prayers recited between the takbīrs.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: The utterance of 'Allāhu Akbar' within the funeral prayer.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Here, the funeral salat and its supplicatory components.
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزِ: Funerals or deceased persons over whom the funeral salat is performed.
key_terms.خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: Five takbīrs forming the funeral prayer structure.

ai.seo_question: How many takbīrs are there in salat over the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the structure of the funeral salat: it consists of five takbīrs, with four supplicatory prayers between them. The apparent difference in the Imam’s عليه السلام answers is resolved by distinguishing between the number of takbīrs and the number of prayers within the rite.
